clue.text: Overseas budget's foremost, in a way

indicators.note: the word in tells us one piece sits inside the phrase that follows it

parts.note: a way is A ROAD, a road being a way to travel

indicators.note: foremost asks for the leading letter of the word budget

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a holiday overseas is, in some way, dictated by the budget.
explanation.definitionFit: Being overseas means being in a foreign country, out of one's homeland, which is the adverb's sense.

clue.text: Speedos for one newfangled cab, we hear

indicators.note: newfangled means made in a novel, unfamiliar way, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone comments that a novel style of taxi is being worn, as though swimwear were a cab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' looks like a sound-alike signal, but those letters simply join CAB as the material to rearrange. Speedos are a brand of tight swimming trunks.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedos are swimming trunks, an example of clothing worn on the sand by the sea, hence 'for one'.

clue.text: Part of rock formation cut off more than the rest?

definitions.meaning: a mass of bedrock that sticks up through the soil at the surface

definitions.text: cut off more than the rest
definitions.meaning: read whimsically as to ..., that is crop or trim more than others do, like outdo or outrun

explanation.surface: A geologist asks whether one piece of a rock formation was cut away more than the others.
explanation.definitionFit: Geologically it names an exposed portion of bedrock; the second reading coins a verb on the pattern of outdo, meaning to clip more.

clue.text: Last of all, removed unsightly urine stain

indicators.note: last of all asks for the final letter of every one of the following words

explanation.surface: Someone reports that at last an ugly urine stain has been cleaned away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last of all' reads as 'finally' in the story but takes the end letter of each of the three words that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A dye is a colouring that stains fabric, so as a verb or noun it matches stain.

clue.text: Miss going around star's place in America

indicators.note: going around says the girl's word wraps itself about the star's name

parts.note: a miss is a young woman, a lass
Vega is a bright star in the constellation Lyra; the 's is a linking 'is'

explanation.surface: A young woman travels round a celebrity's home somewhere in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'star' suggests a film star, but it is the actual star Vega, which LASS goes around.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nevada gambling city is a location in the United States, matching a place in America.

clue.text: Row over new bedclothes perhaps

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the first piece above the second

parts.note: a row is a line

explanation.surface: An argument erupts over new bedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel, but it means a line of things.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheets and pillowcases are household textiles collectively called by this fabric's name, so bedclothes are an example.

clue.text: Time for trivial news, one ass implied?

parts.note: read the answer's second word as fodder and its first word as an anagram signal: rearranging the six letters of the last word gives the clue words one ass

explanation.surface: A newspaper's quiet period is mocked: is one fool behind it?
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer works as an instruction ('silly' signalling rearrangement), and carrying it out on the second word yields ONE ASS, which 'implied' hints at.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the late-summer lull when newspapers fill pages with frivolous stories for want of hard news.

clue.text: Struggling to hear, getting outside of this finally?

definitions.text: Struggling to hear, getting outside of this finally?

indicators.note: getting outside of says the rearranged letters wrap around the single letter that follows
struggling suggests letters thrashing about into a new order
finally takes the end letter of the word this

explanation.surface: Someone straining to catch sounds has moved beyond the range where hearing is possible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Struggling' rearranges TO HEAR into EARHOT, which then goes round S, the last letter of 'this'. The whole clue also defines: whoever strains to hear has got out of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means the distance within which sound can be heard, so struggling to hear means one is beyond it.

clue.text: Daphne paid regularly in advance

indicators.note: regularly asks for every other letter of the two words, taken at even intervals

explanation.surface: Daphne habitually settled her bills before they were due.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' seems to say how often Daphne paid; it picks the 2nd, 4th, 6th, 8th and 10th letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Being before or in front in time or position is exactly the phrase in advance.

clue.text: Strongly criticise article about memorial

parts.note: to pan a show is to slate it
the is the definite article
on can mean about, as in a talk on art

explanation.surface: Someone attacks a newspaper piece about a monument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' seems to be a newspaper piece; it is the grammatical article THE.
explanation.definitionFit: A building honouring a nation's illustrious dead, such as the one in Paris, serves as a memorial.

clue.text: Right for first daughter, to run food store

indicators.note: for first says the opening instance of one letter is swapped for another

parts.note: a run in tights is a ladder
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper puts the right person in place of the elder daughter to manage a grocery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run' looks like 'manage', but it is a ladder in stockings; its first D becomes R.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantry or cool room for keeping provisions is a store for food.

clue.text: Fellow is after tea? No, wine

indicators.note: is after places the fellow's word following the tea's

parts.note: char is British slang for tea
a don is a fellow of a university college
nay is an old word for no

explanation.surface: A man wants something stronger than tea: not that, wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A white grape variety and the dry white wine made from it.

clue.text: Old bass has fish smell, going past sell-by date

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bass in music
sole is a flatfish
a scent is a smell

explanation.surface: An old sea bass that smells of fish has gone off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bass' looks like the fish, but it is the musical voice, abbreviated B.
explanation.definitionFit: Becoming outdated and passing out of use is like a product passing the date by which it should be sold.

clue.text: Pelt Henry with fish

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Someone is told to throw fish at a man named Henry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pelt' looks like a verb (to bombard) but is the noun, an animal's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal's skin with fur on is a pelt, a synonym.

clue.text: Pee-pee or leak

parts.note: wee is a childish word for urine or urinating
P is the abbreviation for a penny, pronounced pee

explanation.surface: A nursery euphemism for urinating is equated with taking a leak.
explanation.walkthrough: The two halves of the nursery word work differently: one is a synonym, the other is the name of the letter P, as in pence.
explanation.definitionFit: To ooze or seep liquid, as a wound or wall does, is a sense of leak.

clue.text: Meandering river confined inside another

indicators.note: inside places the first pieces within the second river's name

parts.note: another river, here the Seine in France
pent, as in pent-up, means shut in

explanation.surface: A winding river is enclosed within a second one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' means another river: the Seine.
explanation.definitionFit: Snakelike and winding, so a course that wanders back and forth is meandering.

clue.text: Paper trail initially lost

indicators.note: initially lost says the opening letter of the synonym goes missing

parts.note: to drag is to trail along the ground

explanation.surface: A paper trail has been lost from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paper trail' reads as one phrase but splits: 'Paper' is the definition, 'trail' is DRAG.
explanation.definitionFit: A rag is a slang, disparaging word for a newspaper, especially a tabloid.

clue.text: Hipster in for treatment — it's a kidney problem

indicators.note: for treatment suggests the letters are worked over and processed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A trendy young man is admitted for care with a renal complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for treatment' looks medical, which fits the surface, but it signals the letters of HIPSTER IN being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The medical term means inflammation of the kidneys, so it is a renal disorder.

clue.text: Toilets placed around stage will offer advantages

indicators.note: placed around says the toilets' word is put round the stage's word

parts.note: privies are outdoor toilets
a leg is a stage of a journey or race

explanation.surface: Lavatories installed around a theatre stage will give it an edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stage' suggests a theatre, but it is a leg of a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Special rights or benefits enjoyed by a few are advantages.

clue.text: Courageous fighter stops vehicle on time

indicators.note: in a down clue, on places the first part above the next
stops means plugs, so the fighter fills a gap in the vehicle

parts.note: a van is a vehicle
Muhammad Ali, the boxer

explanation.surface: A brave warrior halts a vehicle punctually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Courageous fighter' looks like one phrase but splits: the boxer Ali goes inside VAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: brave, bold and showing courage.

clue.text: Scruff going about in threadbare pants

indicators.note: going about says the letters turn round and read backwards
in says the letters lie within the words threadbare pants

explanation.surface: A scruffy person wanders around in worn-out trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scruff' looks like a scruffy person, but it is the scruff of the neck. 'in' finds EPAN across the two words; 'going about' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The scruff is the back of the neck, the same part as the nape.

clue.text: Company supports mounting Caribbean opera

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece that supports another sits beneath it
mounting, in a down clue, says the word climbs and so reads from bottom to top

parts.note: Cuban, from the Caribbean island of Cuba

explanation.surface: A business backs the staging of a West Indian opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caribbean' is CUBAN, which 'mounting' turns upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdi's early opera about the Babylonian king Nebuchadnezzar is an example of the form.

clue.text: Buddy takes first bit of ladies' wear off

parts.note: a pal is a friend or buddy

indicators.note: first bit of asks for the opening letter of ladies'

explanation.surface: A friend removes the top layer of women's clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wear' looks like clothes in the surface, but 'wear off' is a verb meaning to lose its appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: When a novelty begins to pall it grows tiresome and loses its charm, as an effect wears off.

clue.text: Australian PM's spoken? Wow!

indicators.note: spoken says the word sounds like the one before it

parts.note: Theresa May was a UK Prime Minister; May's is said like a puzzle labyrinth

explanation.surface: An exclamation at what an Australian prime minister has said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Australian PM' reads as one person; it is A plus a separate British prime minister, Theresa May.
explanation.definitionFit: Wow, used as a verb, means to astonish or astound someone.

clue.text: Gossip's about entertaining northern composer and playwright

indicators.note: entertaining means holding a guest, so one piece goes inside the other
about says the word turns round and reads backwards

parts.note: dirt is gossip; the 's adds an S
Alban Berg, the Austrian composer

explanation.surface: Gossip circulates about a northern composer and dramatist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses DIRTS into STRID, which takes in N, then Berg follows. 'composer and playwright' looks like one person; the composer is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: August Strindberg was a Swedish dramatist, author of Miss Julie.

clue.text: Victor disrupts dance party

indicators.note: disrupts means breaks into, so one letter goes inside the dance

parts.note: a reel is a Scottish dance
Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A man called Victor breaks up a dance party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dance party' reads as one phrase; 'dance' is REEL and 'party' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To revel is to celebrate noisily, so it means to party.

clue.text: Relish announcement of secretary's demise?

parts.note: a PA is a personal assistant, a secretary
late means dead, so the secretary's demise is the PA being late

explanation.surface: An official notice reports the death of a secretary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relish' looks like a verb or a pickle, but it is a sense of taste. 'announcement of' frames the two words as a death notice.
explanation.definitionFit: A palate is a sense of taste, so it means relish in the sense of appreciation.

clue.text: Speed limits for vehicle? 50 round urban area

indicators.note: limits for asks for the outside letters of vehicle

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for 50
O is round in shape
a city is an urban area

explanation.surface: A road sign question: is the speed limit 50 around town?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speed limits' reads as one phrase; it splits into 'Speed' and 'limits', which takes the outer letters V and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Velocity is rate of motion, a synonym for speed.

clue.text: Boy has rising pulse

indicators.note: rising, in a down clue, says the word reads upwards

parts.note: dal is a pulse such as lentils

explanation.surface: A boy's heart rate is going up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulse' looks like a heartbeat but is an edible seed: dal is lentils.
explanation.definitionFit: Lad is an informal word for a boy or young man.

clue.text: Out late, imbibing dram after last of wine? Unlikely, being this

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so one piece goes inside the other
out means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged
after places the dram after the letter from wine
last of takes the final letter of wine

parts.note: a tot is a small drink, a dram

explanation.surface: Someone out late drinking whisky after wine is hardly a non-drinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out late' looks like a night on the town, but 'Out' is the rearrangement signal; 'imbibing' puts the wine's last letter and the dram inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone drinking late is unlikely to be abstinent from alcohol, so the definition points at the abstainer.

clue.text: Sleepy and Doc returned without Bashful, heartlessly

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a Word doc is a document made in Microsoft Word

indicators.note: without backs up heartlessly, saying the shy word goes minus something
heartlessly says the middle letter of the shy word goes

parts.note: bashful means shy

explanation.surface: Three of Snow White's seven dwarfs are mentioned, one of them returning.
explanation.walkthrough: Sleepy, Doc and Bashful look like the dwarfs, but 'Doc' is a Word file, turned round by 'returned', and 'without ... heartlessly' trims the middle H from SHY.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling as if one could nod off is being sleepy, a synonym.
